utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, let the witness stand to take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you'd like to take a seat. Yes, Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Mikulicic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Santic.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On behalf of the defence of Mr. Mario Cerkez, I will put some questions to you. We will talk about events in which you participated. I would like to ask you to try to remember these events as best you can, and when answering my questions to make a small pause and not to speak too fast so that the interpreters can do their job. For the record, would you please introduce yourself and tell us the year and place of your birth.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: My name is Vlado Santic. I live in Santici, the Vitez municipality. I was born on the 31st of January, 1955.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Santic, you are a Croat by nationality?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Roman Catholic?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have dual citizenship of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of school did you graduate from?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: From the chemical vocational school, it's a secondary school. After that, I went to another two-year postsecondary school, also chemical school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you are a qualified chemist?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you serve in the former JNA?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When and where?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: In 1974 in Valjevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get any military rank after your service?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever have any professional military duties while you were working?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No, only the usual exercises that the former army required.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Santic, you are married and have three children?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Formally, you are employed in the Vitezit factory but you don't go to work because there is, in fact, no work?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were born in Vitez and that you live in Santici?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order to represent the places you will talk about during your testimony, I will ask the usher to put a map on the ELMO, that's Z2271. Mr. Santic, to begin with, would you show us the village of Santici and the approximate location of your house.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: It's here, approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your house to the north or to the south of the road running from Vitez in the direction of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: It's on the south side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. We will need this map later, so it can stay on the ELMO. You were living in your own family house?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With your family?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After graduating from secondary school, where did you get a job?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: I got a job in the Vitezit factory in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until when did you work in that factory?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: What do you mean, until when?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about the period before the war.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, until about the 15th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, there were some problems. There was no production. There were difficult conditions. It was wintertime. There was no work. Almost everyone was sent home; only one group was allowed to remain for the maintenance of the factory, and the others were sent home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the factory, in fact, stopped working because of a shortage of raw materials and because there was no market.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people were sent home on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: More than 90 per cent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the ethnic makeup of the employees in Vitezit?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: It was, well, about 50/50, Croats and Muslims. There were some Serbs but not so many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the workers were sent home, was the criterion that was applied ethnic, or were people sent home regardless of their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, they were not actually made redundant. They were just told to wait for work, and we all reported to work. Everyone was involved in some kind of army, and they didn't come to work. Those who stayed behind did go to the factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So in late 1992 you came home, you stopped going to work, and then you became active in the village. What did you do?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, there were village patrols which we organised on our own initiative to guard the roads leading into the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These village guards were organised before you lost your work or after that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, before that, but I didn't participate because I was still working.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Santic, please tell us, what was the ethnic makeup of your village, Santici?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, it was very mixed. Around my house, one house would be Croat, the next house would be Muslim. It's really very mixed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These village guards that were organised, were they also of a mixed composition or not?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, for awhile they were mixed, but then that stopped and the Muslims had their own guards and we had our own guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have explained to us the purpose of these guards. You said you guarded the roads leading into the village. Tell us, Mr. Santic, were your village guards organised by someone outside the village, or was it the villagers themselves? What was the situation?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, we all got together and elected a kind of commander amongst ourselves, and so we organised it on our own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you elected your own commander amongst yourselves.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of you were involved in the village guards in late 1992?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, about 30 of us, maybe a few men more or less. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any weapons?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, there were some weapons, although not all of us were armed. When someone was on duty, he would have a weapon. There were even hunting rifles that we used. But we went home without weapons mostly, because there was a house where we gathered and where we changed shifts and exchanged information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you would simply hand over weapons to one another because there were not enough weapons for everyone.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any uniforms?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Most of us did not. Some people did. Some had parts of uniforms; others had no uniforms at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have just told us, Mr. Santic, that you elected the commander of the village guard amongst yourselves. Would the commander elected stay for a long time, or did they change?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, there were changes. People would be dissatisfied, and then we would come together. There were changes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of you were on duty in one shift?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, five or six of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your main task was?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: To guard the entrances to the village, to go around the village once or twice during a shift.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What conclusion did you come to you, Mr. Santic? What was the main reason for the establishment of these village guards? And why were you guarding the roads leading into the village?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, because the conflict with the Serbs had started, and our people went in the direction of Jajce, Travnik. We were afraid of raids by Serb forces and the JNA on our village; there was always a danger that they might break through and surprise us, and that was mostly why we organised this. There was some looting also, so that was another reason to watch over the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not far from your village, Mr. Santic, is the mountain called Kuber; is that correct? Would you be so kind as to show us on the map the exact location of that mountain.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Would the technical -- oh, thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is the mountain of Kuber.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, in relation to the surroundings, does that mountain command a dominant position, a view?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, Mr. Santic, at that time did you also go to Kuber?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes. We would go and stay there for a week at a time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your task, then, when you went to Mount Kuber?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, there was an elevation there and we were afraid that the Serbian forces could break through and take it. We were also afraid that helicopters might land there, because there were fields there. It was an elevation, and that was the reason why we went up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was this organised, these departures to Mount Kuber? Which of the village guards went to Kuber?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, it was village by village. Our village of Santici went on the 13th, and the whole group was from our village. Then we were replaced by a group from another village, for example, Dubravica, Nadioci, Rijeka. It would always be men from a certain village that would be up there, and they had their commander and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, Mr. Santic, these shifts on Mount Kuber, were they organised in the same way as the village guards? Did you agree among yourselves from the different villages, or was it organised from outside?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, we, from these villages, Rijeka, Nadioci, and so on, we went there; others didn't. So we agreed and then, village by village, would go there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you agreed amongst yourselves?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. How many men would there be in a shift when you went to Mount Kuber?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: About 10 or 11 men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your main task to observe, to reconnoitre?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, we had a few trenches there. They weren't real trenches, but there was a canvas kind of tent there. And that's where we spent our time. We didn't walk around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Santic, that position on Mount Kuber, did your Muslim neighbours go there also?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But not together with you, they went separately?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: They had a position 200 or 300 metres away from our position, above us, higher up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In late 1992 and early 1993, did you have any agreements with your Muslim neighbours on Kuber? Did you have joint shifts or were the organisations separate?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: The organisation was separate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the situation with weapons up there? Were you all armed or did you hand over weapons to one another the way you did in the villages?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, those who did not have a rifle would take someone else's rifle in order to go there. That's what I did too. But when we were there, we were all armed although these were just ordinary rifles, M-48s. There was some automatic weapons but that was very rare.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier in your testimony that in April you went to Kuber. You mentioned the date. Would you repeat it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: We went on the 13th of April. It was Tuesday. I remember very well because we would change shifts on Tuesdays, and we would be there from one Tuesday to another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was the shift from your particular village, the village of Santici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether at that time when you took up your shift on Tuesday the 13th of April, 1993, up until the 16th of April when there was an escalation in the fighting in Vitez and the surrounding areas, do you remember whether at Kuber there was an incident that took place of any kind?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes. Not that same day but one or two days later when we were up there. There was some shooting, and the shooting lasted for perhaps an hour. We didn't see anything, we just heard the shooting. And it wasn't continuous, it was just sporadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you hear the shooting come from; from what direction?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: They told us that it was from the village of Bilivode, that that was what the village was called on the road to Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you heard shooting but you didn't know what was actually going on; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear about it later on, what the shooting was all about and what had actually happened?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: They told us that the Muslims had attacked a portion of us Croats who were on patrol in the area and that a conflict had arisen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything more about that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: I think that somebody was either wounded or killed, some of the Croats, but I forget who. I don't know about the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but that was before the 16th, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was one or two days before the 16th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that incident and after that shooting, over the next day or two up until the 16th, there were no further incidents, were there?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened on the 16th, in the morning?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: On the morning of the 16th, I think that it was about twenty to 6.00 in the morning, we were awoken. Some of us were up at our positions, and others were in a shed below, a hut below, but there was -- it was rather misty so you couldn't see anything properly and there was some shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you say where the shooting was coming from?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, below us, you could hear it better but it was coming from all around and we weren't able to actually pinpoint the direction it was coming from and didn't know what was actually going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that it was foggy at that time?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, it was rather misty. We couldn't determine what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any information at that time as to what was happening?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Our commander tried to get some information on his Motorola but we went up to our positions, and it was only later that we heard something about it and we were -- visibility was better one hour later too so we could see better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your commander tried to learn what was going on through this radio transmitter; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, and he received information that there had been a conflict down in our village, but he wasn't able to tell us straight away what was happening. That was only later. It was only when the fog had lifted that we were able to see that around our houses, and my house in particular, because we were all local inhabitants, we saw that houses were burning and we couldn't quite make out whether it was my house or whose house it actually was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when the fog lifted, you saw that in the region of your village, the village of Santici, houses were on fire; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see the village of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, we saw them burning. We couldn't actually see Ahmici because it's more difficult to see them. We were further off from the road so it's easier to see our village, but we did see some houses on fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that there were about ten of you in the shift. Did you all remain in your positions?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, as we were upset to see what was happening down below, we sent two of our men to go and see what was happening to our families, and two men went off to see how they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about you personally?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: I stayed up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was your commanding officer at that position?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: It was Zeljo Livancic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a member of your village guard as well?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he was a person whom you selected among yourselves to be the commander?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The two men that went off from Kuber down to the village, did they come back and tell you what was going on?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did they come back?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: They returned several hours later. They just went to see whether our families were all right and asked about all our families and then came back up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: They said that the Muslim houses were burning and that our families were alive and well, and they returned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that particular day, were there any armed conflicts at Kuber at the positions that you were in?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Only later on, perhaps in the morning hours, shooting started. The Muslims started targeting us and then we took refuge, took cover, because there is a hill there, and there were a few trenches; three, in fact, not many trenches. So after their shooting, we returned fire. And this went on for a couple of hours perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From which direction did the Muslims fire at you?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: From Zenica where they held the positions. That's where that shooting came from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those the same people that held positions as village guards, the positions that you spoke about a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, probably. I can't tell you for sure because they had already moved. After the events that had taken place in Ahmici or from wherever, there was no further contact. And before that, we would meet where there was a source, a water source, a water spring. We would meet there and talk there, but afterwards there was no further contact of that kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that you came under fire from snipers with fragmentation bullets. Was there any heavier shooting afterwards?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: I think in the afternoon hours there was a stronger attack from the Vrhovine area. That was a hill. It's not very high, but there's a lot of growth so you can hide yourself, and that's where the attack came from and along from this attack, from the Zenica direction, from the north.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, Mr. Santic, were there any grenades, any shelling?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes. First one, and then more shelling next to the trench I was in, but luckily it was a good trench that we had dug several days ago, but a grenade fell right in front of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any wounded?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Two of our men stayed up at Kuber and Zeljo Livancic, the commander, was killed on the occasion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to determine the direction from which the shelling was coming?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: I think it was from Vrhovine, as far as I was able to see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you point the area out to us on the map, please.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Vrhovine is up here and it was to the left. That's where the shelling took place. Vrhovine is here. There's a small hill there, and we were to the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who held that position?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: The Muslims held that position, and we didn't go there. We stood guard towards that village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that three of your neighbours were killed on one occasion and amongst them one of your commanders, Zeljo Livancic. What intensity was that attack?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, it was a strong attack with artillery support, as I mentioned a moment ago. And I saw that when we were withdrawing, a larger group had entered the area where that other trench was where Livancic and Grkic were, and we had to withdraw. I cannot tell you exactly how many people there were, but I saw at least ten, more than ten people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of you were there?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: There were ten of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were forced to withdraw; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show us on the map your route when you withdrew?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: From the Kratine area, we went right down quite low and the next day we saw that there wasn't an all-out attack, but here, Kratine and Gola Kosa, that's the spot. That's the locality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The position you are pointing to, Kratine, that is part of Mount Kuber, the slopes of Mount Kuber; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at the difference in altitude, how much lower is it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, it is a couple of hundred metres lower, the altitude.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the breadth of the area?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Three or four kilometres, I would say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was your new defensive position, was it not?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do once you had reached that position?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: When we got there, we deployed so as to set up a defence towards the village, and we separated out some 500 or 600 metres. But there wasn't an attack on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there were very few of you. If I can count properly, there were only seven of you because three had been killed?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any reinforcements?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, the next day and the day after, we would receive some reinforcements. The line took 15 days to set up because people from Vitez came to join us who had been mobilised to help defend the defence line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your neighbours from the village guard in Santici who were not up there with you, did they come to help you out?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No, they deployed around different parts of the village of Santici, Krtina Mahala and so on they were in that region. They spread out there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were more exposed, your point was further out than the defence line for the village of Santici itself; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there was no attack on your defence line?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No, there was not. For several days, I can't tell you exactly but not during those few days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were at Kratine, you had taken up the positions there, together with your neighbours; all the members of the village guard were there. Were there any military units? Did anybody from a military unit come to inform you as to what your assignments were and what you should do?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, they were our neighbours from Nadioci, because their village was -- this was more important for their village. Just to prevent them from entering our villages, our particular village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me repeat my question. Perhaps you didn't understand me. Did anybody from the military structures of Vitez, the Vitez Brigade, for example, reach you at your positions and give instructions as to what your assignments and duties were?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened next? Time passed, and what happened?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, with each passing day, the line became better fortified. There were no attacks. There was just sporadic gunfire or the odd grenade would fall close to our positions, but there was no all-out attack from the Kuber area. We noticed that the Muslims had moved further up too and were digging in there. So that there was sporadic gunfire. But we were able to fortify our defence line better because people came in over the next 15 days and we were able to complete our defence strategy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. But at one particular point, sometime later, you were given military ID cards, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps a month or two went by when we got our military ID cards and we knew that we were members of the Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Santic, could you describe to us how this came about, briefly? How were these military ID cards distributed?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, someone from the command came by, and our commander distributed these ID cards to us. They had our names on them and denoted our membership in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did it actually say on these cards?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: That we had become members of the Vitez Brigade, so that we could know exactly who we belonged to as regards military formation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These ID cards, you say, were distributed by your commander. Who gave him the ID cards; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly whether it was a commander whose name was Bertovic. I think it was him. He brought them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to remember, Mr. Santic, which unit you belonged to, in keeping with what it said on that military ID card?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: The Vitez Brigade. I don't know what else it said. I've forgotten. Perhaps I've got it at home somewhere. But that's more or less what it said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, Mr. Santic, what happened next? Were you at that position throughout the time, or did you change positions?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, until the end of the war I held that position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a moment ago that this defence line, this position, was fortified little by little. When you came to that position for the first time, were there any trenches that had been dug?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No, nothing had been dug there yet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After your arrival, did you start digging in?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the beginning there were seven of you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, seven at first. But the number grew with each passing day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you start digging the trenches yourselves to begin with?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Afterwards were you assisted in this task by anybody?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, the Muslims would come too, the Muslims from Vitez. I know some of the people who came. There were some Romanies amongst them as well, and there were some of our own people. My father, for one. He was an elderly man; he was 63 years old at the time. But he came to help us out, and so did some other people. But that took place later on, after, say, about ten days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people who came to help you out in digging these trenches, did they come in an organised fashion? Were they brought there, escorted by anybody?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: The people from the military police brought them. They would stay up there during the day and were taken back by vans or buses, so that they would go back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that the men who helped dig had been brought in a van, escorted by the military police, does that cover both Croats, including your father, and Muslims, or only Muslims?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Muslims were brought by the military police. Our men volunteered and came on their own. They knew where.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity - you say that you knew some of the Muslims who were brought there, escorted by the military police. Did you have any opportunity to talk to those people?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, but not much because the situation, after all, was tense. But we'd offer them something, a cigarette or ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps see anyone harass those Muslims, beat, ill-treat them at the positions there?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: While they were at the positions there, nobody harassed them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they complain that somebody mistreated them elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: They did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that even your father, who was 63 at the time, also came to dig.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that an isolated case, or were there more such instances?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Quite a number. I know various of our neighbours, mostly elderly and even those who did not even serve the former army for various reasons, even they came up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Throughout the time while you were keeping your positions, any one of those individuals who came to help dig trenches, was any one of them injured, wounded, or anything?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Any one of us up there, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that they were brought there by some buses of the military police, and the military police also took them away as it had brought them up there.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During their stay at the positions, did the military police stay by them or not?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No, there was no military police. We were the only ones who were with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Santic, you already told us in the beginning that your village was practically very near the village of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that your village was to the south of the road; you showed it to us on the map. The village of Ahmici is, for the most part, on what part of the road?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, for the most part, it is to the north of the road, even though there is a part of the village which is below the road or, rather, to the south of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You also told us that at the beginning the village guards were mixed. Were there any significant incidents between you, the villagers, I mean Croats and Muslims, prior to the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: As for our villagers, no. Between our villagers there were no incidents to speak of. Only when the Muslims tried to block a unit which was to take its shift on Jajce - it also was near my village - then there was a fighting which broke out. But not from our village, on the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you referring to the event that happened in late 1992?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Chamber has already heard a great deal of testimony about that incident so that I will not ask you any questions. But if need be, you can answer the Prosecutor's questions about this.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Quite. No problem, if I know the answers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the beginning of your testimony, you also said that you were in the Vitezit and that the ethnic composition of workers there was roughly 50/50. What were you there?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: I was shop steward.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your duty was to register the attendance at work, was it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember if the management of the plant or you yourself asked the workers of Muslim origin to sign some statements of allegiance, of loyalty, to the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No. Nothing like that existed there that anyone had to pronounce himself, or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps observe any major layoffs or firing of Muslims from work?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Santic, you described to us your participation in these events where you recognised your military service.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, in a manner of speaking, because we were issued those certificates, we, the participants, members of the village guards. And the date was put, I believe it was the month of April 1993 -- no, 1992, and it was a kind of a tribute paid to us by way of these certificates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get those certificates?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: We did, yes. I believe from the 8th of April, and then until, I don't know, roughly four years of service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever use them?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No. It's just a piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, Mr. Santic, when were you demobilised? When did you leave your military unit?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: I think it must have been about four years later after that date, so I think it was 1997. Because we went to defence lines against the Serbs up there, and that part was also registered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean after the conflict in the Lasva Valley?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registrar - I'm sorry I forgot to announce it earlier - show the witness Exhibit Z70.2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Santic, I will now show you this list which was adduced as an exhibit and which is a list of persons who took part in the organised resistance against the aggression in various villages in the Vitez municipality. Your village is also there. I should invite you to comment on one item on that list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I would ask the usher to turn to page 18.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Santic, will you please look at number 18 here.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says Vlado (Jozo) Santic, isn't it? Your father's name Jozo, is it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Santic, what does this number here mean?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: This is the citizen's number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Chamber has already heard the first two digits mean the date of birth, following it is the month, and the three following figures the year of birth. So it means that this person, Vlado Santic, son of Jozo, was born on the 10th of September 1996 [sic]. Is that you?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look then at the signature to your right. Do you recognise this signature? It says Anna Santic, I think?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No there are no Annas in my family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is evidently some other Santic, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, obviously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Even though his father is the namesake of your father?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Quite.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you Mr. Santic. This concludes my examination, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Kordic Defence has no questions for this witness. Cross-examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Santic, just before we turn to matters of detail and history, let's see if I understand it. You were on the Kuber feature from the 13th of April until when continuously?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: The end of the war between the Muslims and Croats. It ended in negotiations, so until -- I believe it was the 13th again, 13th of April 1994 when I came down from Kuber and turned over my weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in that intervening year, are you saying that you personally never once went back to your village of Santici?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: That's not what I said. We would go home now and then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. The remainder of your family, your wife, your children, they were still in Santici, were they?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: They were in Santici, but not throughout. They had also -- they also left the house on several occasions and for several days at a time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But they were there, for example, on the night of the 13th, 14th, 15th and 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You now live with your family still in Santici, or have you moved? I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's where I live.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so there remain in Santici, like your family, a number of Croats who were there on the night of the 15th and 16th and they're still living there in Santici?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to deal with the geography, it's pretty clear from the map but you can confirm for us the villages of Dubravica, Santici, Nadioci and Ahmici, they all merge pretty much one into the next, don't they?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Santici -- sorry, the road that runs from Dubravica east by those villages is a sort of gently undulating road. It goes up and down a little bit, over the hills. It's not entirely flat, correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Correct. It's not flat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Santici is a slightly larger village, I suspect, though I haven't checked the statistics, but it's a slightly larger village and it's a sort of village that has one shop or a couple of shops on the main road to service your requirements?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, quite.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it hasn't got any major shops so that for your major shopping you'd go either to the shops in Dubravica or right through to Vitez; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes. These are all small shops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course the factory is the other side of the town of Vitez, lying, as we all know, between Veceriska and Gacice?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you regularly, either with work or out of work, had to go to Vitez throughout 1992 and 1993, and the beginning of 1993?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, almost on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You've spoken of the decline in work at the factory. Was the general impression being given that it was very badly managed, that factory, that it was losing work?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Not that it was poorly run, but there were difficulties. It was difficult to bring in the production material because it mostly came from Croatia, and there was a problem with the passage. And I should say it was due to wartime conditions outside Vitez and its environs, but they nevertheless affected the production.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by the autumn of 1992, what percentage of the work force was still working at the factory, measured in terms of, I don't know, full production in 1991 or 1990; what percentage was left with a job in the autumn of 1992?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Before that, there were two shifts. At that time, there was only one shift working, so about one half of the staff continued to work until the production ground to a halt, and that was in late 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because, you see, you've been asked questions about whether people were required to -- how was it expressed -- give certificates of loyalty in order to retain their jobs, but by the end of 1992, pretty nearly everybody had lost their job in any case, hadn't they, because production had ground to a halt?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, it simply came to a stop. I mean it did not work. There were only -- I don't know, security guards were still there, perhaps some commercial department here and there, but the production had completely stopped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you were, yourself, without work?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am just going to ask you a few questions about 1992, see what your visits to the town and your passage through the town will have provided you by way of information. You were aware, of course, that the HZ HB existed, were you, the community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, naturally there was media and what we heard in the media, that's what we knew about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were aware, were you, that the HVO was effectively taking over the town in 1992 because, of course, it was setting up checkpoints, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: There were some checkpoints but there were also checkpoints on the Muslim side, because, for instance, in Mahala where there were Muslim barricades. So there were barricades on both sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of the HVO taking over the municipal building, for example, at one stage?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: I think that both did it. I don't know. I didn't go there very often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Altogether, how many factories were there in Vitez? We've heard about the big factory, but that wasn't the only factory. Were there some other factories?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, there were. There was Impregnacija, there was the public utilities company. Well, it's Nova Bila already, but it's -- yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About some nine major factories, would that be about right? We can list them later if it's necessary but would you accept in general terms that that's about right?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know exactly, but could be, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you aware of the fact that of those factories, all bar one, were taken over by the HVO? You were a person with a shop steward's experience. All the factories, bar one, were taken over by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Did you go to the oath-taking ceremony in the summer of 1992 for the HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on to October of 1992 by which time you were pretty well out of work; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: October 1992? No, that's not when I lost my job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You still had a job then. Were you aware of any incident in your village - for the Chamber's benefit, this is Witness U, pages 10.192 and onwards. Were you aware of an incident in your village about the 18th of or 20th of October where a 19-year-old Muslim got killed?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: That day I was supposed to go to work, and I was awakened by shooting when it broke out. I think it was in the morning. And later, I heard that this Muslim had been killed. I knew him personally. And even my Muslim neighbours came to my house. We were there together. We were afraid so we stuck together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who - was it Nenad Santic who was involved?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was it then from the HVO who killed this 19-year-old boy?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you. I know that a conflict did break out, but I only learnt about it later. You are probably referring to the case when the soldiers were supposed to go in the direction of Jajce and Travnik where they were holding the position against the Serbs and they think that there was a conflict among them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it's right, isn't it, that this incident in which the 19-year-old boy died was an incident where the HVO were effectively attacking Santici? That's where people were so frightened.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know who attacked whom, I can't answer that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a sort of - I don't mean this in any sense offensively; on the contrary, it's probably very charming - this is a one-cafe town, isn't it, or a one-cafe village, so that we get the picture of the place. And you're really telling us you can't give us any help with who it was killed this innocent young man?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: I can't say because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware later on in -- well, about the same time, actually, a couple of days later, that all Muslims were required to hand their weapons over? That was a requirement made of them by the man Cerkez, were you aware of that, in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: I don't know that they all handed over their weapons or that someone ordered that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have some recollection of the HVO requiring that the Muslims should be disarmed? Think back, please.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: I don't know because I just said that I was also working at that time, and until things quieted down. When they did, I went back to work for a while, and I wasn't involved. I only started participating in all of this when we stopped working.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You tell us that there were Muslims still at work, and you were the shop steward, and you drove through Vitez every day. Can you really not help us --

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Up until the last day when I was working, there were Muslims working with me. There were people from Ahmici who went to work with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then just, I think, the last question for 1992, a number of coffee shops and restaurants and so on belonging to Muslims were blown up in Vitez, weren't they, by HVO soldiers. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: I know that there were bombings of cafes. I think it wasn't only the Muslim cafes were blown up, but I can add that groups of soldiers would come from Mostar who were disorderly and who caused problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were their names, and what was the name of the group you say were causing problems?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Bruno Busic, I think, and Pavlovic. It was those units from Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the HVO were controlling the town. What did they say they were doing about it or were they, in fact, welcoming these groups? What was it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: I don't think the HVO had control over the town. I just mentioned that parts were under Muslim control, other parts were under Croat control. I don't know, but these groups from Herzegovina finally left Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under HVO direction, perhaps. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's come straight on to these village guards. You say that villages guarded the Kuber feature in turn. Well, if we just measure it on the map, it's about six kilometres, as the crow would fly, from Santici to the top of the Kuber feature. Just tell us, please, how did the replacement of one village guard by another occur?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: You mean how did we go up there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I mean how did one guard know to replace another? It's six kilometres away, communication never that easy. How was it known that your group would be replaced by another village group?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, four or five villages, we organised ourselves and we agreed that a shift should go. And then the commanders we elected among ourselves. For example, Zeljo Livancic was our commander, they kept in touch. And they would agree among themselves which village would go when, and then he would tell the rest of us. He would come to my house or ring me up and tell me we were going on a certain date and then we would gather together before going up together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you see you've been giving a picture as it were entirely independent little village guards or small village guards, and you're now describing, as it were, a cooperative arrangement between the village guard leaders; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I have your answers please on a document that we've looked at before, 653, I thought had I brought my copy with me. If you want to use mine rather than trouble the -- I must suggest to you that there must plainly have been some degree of planning for all this guarding of Kuber by different villages. Perhaps it was planning by the HVO. What do you say to that? Was it planned, this guarding of the Kuber feature, by the HVO? Was there some central planning?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. As I see, the witness was not given the Croatian text, and probably the title of the document is important to understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I thought the Croatian was attached to the English version. My mistake. We'll have to get the proper version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: If I also may ask my dear colleague not to use this document but the one with the translation, because one witness before was confused by that. He told us in the briefing. We didn't realise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While we're getting the document, Mr. Santic, just say again, was there some measure of HVO or Viteska Brigade control of the guarding of the Kuber feature? Was there?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No. We organised it ourselves. We would come together, the representatives of the villages, and discuss it and agree on it. Not all the men but the leaders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, then, just for us, please, here's a document that predates the outbreak of the fighting. It's the 14th of April, 1993, the day after you went up to Kuber. It comes from the Viteska Brigade. It speaks of the 1st Battalion of that Viteska Brigade, and it says that so far as Santici is concerned, it was in the 1st Company, under the commander Slavko Papic, and that there were 12 soldiers there. How would you explain that document to us, please?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: I don't know. We contacted only with Zeljo Livancic. He would come and tell me when we would meet and that we were supposed to go to Kuber.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, you've told us that there were about ten men from your deployment, from your village, guarding the feature at Kuber.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's not 12. But were there, in fact, a maximum of some 12. I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: There would be 12 sometimes. But there were ten of us, because some people had problems and they gave up at the last moment and didn't go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it looks, doesn't it, as though this document, which is a Viteska Brigade document, is identifying the very 12 men from Santici as members of the 1st Company, under the command of Slavko Papic. Now, can you explain how you're given that position before the outbreak of fighting, please?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, the Vitez Brigade had not been established yet. We were simply members of the HVO and the village guards. The village guards were organised on their own initiative. This is not something I'm familiar with; I have not had an opportunity of seeing it before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you told us when you spoke of what happened on the nights or the days that are more important that your commander had a Motorola. Did you ever use that Motorola yourself?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know with whom he was communicating when he was trying to find out, as you say, what had happened in the villages.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, I think he tried to ring up someone in the village. I don't know who else had a Motorola. He tried to contact him from where our houses were, because we asked him to tell us what was going on because we didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, there was a communication centre for the HVO in the centre of Vitez, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Equally, you don't know if your commander was communicating with the Vitez communication centre, do you?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: I think he was contacting someone from the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Please listen to the question. You've already told us you didn't use it yourself. You don't know one way or another --

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- whether he --

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go on a little bit, then, to those events, and I'll be interested -- I'm going to pass over the first quarter of 1993 and I'll just deal with the central events. As I understand your evidence, on the morning of the 16th when, as you say, the fog or the mist cleared, it was obvious that there had been terrible events in your village and also in the village of Ahmici; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: We got the real information when two of our men who went to see what had happened came back. It was only then that we learned, and we learned certain details later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But, Mr. Santic, if you see either your own house or the house next door in flames and you see lots of other houses in flames, it's a pretty terrifying sight, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Of course it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Your wife and children were there.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No. When this friend of mine came back, he said my wife and children were in the next village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, really. Which village was that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: In Donja Rovna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This came as a surprise to you, did it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes. After what had happened there, when I saw that it was burning, I was not surprised to hear that they'd had to flee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you understand it, they fled after the fighting or before, or do you still not know?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: According to what my wife told me, when the shooting started, that was when they fled. That was when.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so that we can see it on the map perhaps, the village to which you have been told your wife fled, Donja Rovna. We can see Rovna all right. Where's Donja Rovna?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Here, where you cross. It's somewhere -- is that the railway track? Well, it's here --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Off the road to --

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: -- about two kilometres from the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Off the road to the south.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, now, let's just go back a little bit. Before you ever got news back from the people who had gone down to the village - I'm not going to ask you for the detail of what they told you, because if those people are alive and well, they can always come and tell them themselves - before they came back, you're telling us that you had no knowledge at all of where your wife and children might have been. They could have been in the village and it could have been your house that was on fire; would that be right?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: They could have been. I didn't know where they were at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And yet you still regard it as your duty to stay on Kuber and not to go down to the village.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: I was serving in the army. I had certain obligations. If I agreed to become a soldier, I could not leave the front line just like that, or my position. Because when I became a soldier, I underwent some training and we had to respect certain rules.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that when you were on the Kuber feature, you were serving as a soldier in accordance with an agreement, it wasn't as a village guard; is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, when a man is carrying a weapon and he has a certain task, he has agreed to become a soldier and he feels like a soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Santic, you've been quite concerned to tell us that the village guards were an informal arrangement. You're now telling us that it was so formal on the night -- the morning of the 16th that you were bound by your duties as a soldier so that you couldn't go down and check on your wife and children? Which is it? Is that really true?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, we had certain obligations because we had gone up there, we had volunteered to go. But still, we did send two people to see what was happening. We didn't know what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before I return to that issue, I'm just going to pick up, for one last question, on your answers about a soldier with obligations. Is the truth revealed in that document you were looking at a few minutes ago; namely, that by this time, before the start of the fighting, you well understood yourself to be a member of the Viteska Brigade, one of the 12 people listed from your village?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: We were not in the Vitez Brigade. It was only later that we were given papers saying we were members of the Vitez Brigade. We were simply members of the HVO and the village guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let me come back to this: You didn't go down. Is that because you knew full well that there was going to be an attack by Croats on Muslims?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: We didn't know at all that there would be an attack or whether there was an attack, or what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, we've had some evidence in this case from a witness called Nura Pezer, transcript 15447 and following, and from another witness, at page 10200, to the effect that before the attack happened, there was pointing out in the village to an unknown man of Muslim houses. Now, I know that you would say that you were on the Kuber feature by the night of the 15th. But one way or another, had you or your commander been informed, perhaps by Motorola, that an attack was about to happen on Muslim properties?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: We didn't know anything. Some people were even sleeping in the shed where we were when the shooting awakened us. They probably wouldn't have gone to sleep if they'd known something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You tell us that you made some returns in the course of this year to your village - again, I'm not going to ask you to tell us what other Santici villagers told you - but when was your first return to your village? How long after the events of the 16th?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: It was about -- well, I was up there for about 15 days non-stop after the 13th, and it was only then that I went home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went back, there was a picture of complete devastation so far as the Muslim houses were concerned, and all the Croat houses were left standing; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Staying with the 16th, it's right, isn't it, that there was no question -- oh, I must just deal with one other matter before I come to the 16th because it's in your evidence and summary. You say there was some incident of fighting before the 16th -- not fighting, of gunfire, before the 16th; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The most you know about it is that you say you heard something from a particular direction. That's the most you know about it yourself.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, at first.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't actually see the gunfire yourself.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No, because it was foggy and we couldn't see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just yes or no. You were told something by someone else, just yes or no to that, something about this incident.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No. Maybe if you tell me when, what time you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us you heard that there was a Muslim attack. "They told us there was a Muslim attack." All I want to know is who the "they" is? Who told you this?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: The people -- a Muslim attack? The information came from the people who came from Bilivode, Croats who came to our positions. They had --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Their names?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: I don't know them because it's not close to us. Maybe I knew their names then, but a lot of time has elapsed and I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. In fact, although it's not in your summary of evidence that you, no doubt, read carefully yesterday, I think you even told the Judges that somebody you understand was killed in this attack. Do you have the name of that person?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you say that this all came from the direction of Bilivode?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: The direction of Bilivode. They say it's a village. I don't know the area in the direction of Zenica very well. I went to the Kuber feature for the first time only when this war broke out; I wasn't familiar with it before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, are you sure there was any such incident in Bilivode before the 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure your memory isn't playing tricks with you?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you can't provide any other names, either of the people who gave you the information or of anyone who was killed?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No, because I don't know those people. They were from other villages. But someone would always pass by and we would talk to them. But I didn't know those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the same position: In the absence of any contemporaneous documents recording the incident as early as the dates given by the witness, I have to challenge it. But I can't take the matter further. I accept that there was an incident on the 17th of April. I'm endeavouring to finish before the break.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Incidentally, I think you suggest that you were forced into a position at Kratine, or you moved to a position at Kratine; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: When we came down from Kuber, we went to Kratine, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of an incident there involving a family of people on a tractor who were killed, I think, by a man called Bralo? Are you aware of that as an incident, or any part of that incident?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As to the people who came to your -- I should have dealt with it in its order, I'm sorry. You speak of some fire on you on the 16th of April; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That happened later in the day than, of course, the attacks on Ahmici and Santici, didn't it; much later in the day?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mid-afternoon?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: A few hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: There was shooting before noon, the dum-dum bullets. That happened then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this is after the attack on what we know to be the Muslim parts of these other villages, and you are quite unable to say what happened to you was in reaction to what happened down below in the valley or not?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: I didn't know yet that was why.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So far as the people who were brought to dig trenches, the ones who came in what you call in your summary "the compulsory work platoon," were brought under guard and they were under compulsion, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when they were obliged to dig trenches, they were exposed, even in your area, to the danger of being fired on by Muslims who, you tell us, might have been likely to attack you?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, just as we were. Because if there was firing, they would take shelter as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But these were Muslim trench diggers compelled to dig trenches in places where they might be fired upon by Muslims; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, we dug together with them and they dug with us, and we took cover together if there was shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that answers that point. Perhaps I can just ask the witness to look at one exhibit and then I'm done. Exhibit 699, and if it's difficult -- thank you. This is a document that's dated the 17th of April at 6.15 in the evening and it comes from Blaskic, and it's to commanders of two units, the Viteska and the Zrinjski, and also to the 4th Military Police and so on. And it speaks of Muslim forces increasing in the area of Kuber because of the safety of the Kaonik-Vitez road with the objective of preventing the enemy from seizing and taking control. He ordered a defence line in the wider area of Kuber with forces of the Viteska Brigade which are then identified. Just two things, really. Was the 17th of April about the first time there was any real question of risk or fighting of any significant type in the Kuber feature?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, there was danger with respect to the events that had already happened, although I've never seen this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this defence line that was being formed by the Viteska Brigade, as far as you can judge looking at this order, the defence line in which you were involved?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: It probably implies something because it's Kratine. It says Kuber here. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it appear that this is the work you were doing under your commander for the time being, you forming --

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: We attempted to organise the defence line up there and that was the objective because we had received reports that some Muslim forces had been observed there and therefore we wanted to organise ourselves as best as possible. We were worried.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
