utterances.text: Your Honour, I think I've finished. If re-examination is going to be after the break, and given that we've come to these witnesses rather late because of -- if I could just keep open the possibility of asking another question after the break, I would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll take the break for half an hour. Mr. Santic, don't speak to anybody about your evidence during the break until it's over. Don't let anybody speak to you about it. Thank you. Yes, we'll sit again just after half past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Just one more very small topic, possibly one more question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Santic, on the 16th of April when the ten of you were up there on Kuber defending it, you were, were you, the only people up there, to your knowledge, defending Kuber at that time?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the only means of communication was the Motorola that your commander had?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if the witness could look, please, at 684 - incidentally this is a document which matches a later-produced, I think, Defence exhibit D92/1 but I'll stick with 684. Now, if you'd look at this document, please, in the original, we'll have the English version on the ELMO. This is an order coming from Blaskic on the 16th at 1945 hours in the evening, and it goes to the Zrinjski Brigade in Busovaca, but that's not what I'm interested in. If you look at the content of the order, Mr. Santic, you'll see that in item one, it's headed for the "Defence of Kuber". Item one is, "Extremist Muslim forces are advancing from Gornji Zenica." And then item two is the task of the Zrinjski Brigade, which is to reinforce the defence of Kuber. And it then says in item three, "You are to coordinate your actions with the Viteska Brigade and make sure that Kuber doesn't fall." Now, in two ways he's referring, really, to the existing defence of Kuber because he says, "You're to reinforce the defence and to coordinate with the Viteska Brigade." Your ten men were the only ten men there defending Kuber, that's correct, you've already told me that, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Blaskic knew, obviously, of the existence of your work there because he speaks of reinforcing what you were doing, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Probably, but we were up there alone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And basically what Blaskic is apparently saying is that will the Zrinjski Brigade from Busovaca join forces with the Viteska Brigade. The Viteska Brigade was you at that time, wasn't it, so far as the Kuber feature was concerned?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Whether it was the Vitez Brigade, whether it was formed at the time or not, I don't know. I learned only later that I was, in fact, a member of the Vitez Brigade. But at that time, and during the attacks, we were up there alone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Responding via your commander and via Vitez to Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. I never saw this document. I'm looking at it for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. Re-examined by Mr. Mikulicic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Mr. Santic, we consider that this matter has not been cleared up sufficiently so I should like to go back to it and the events that you described at the Kuber feature. First of all, an introductory question. The concept of Kuber, the name Kuber, is that the name of a mountain or is it the name of one concentrated spot, place?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Where we were, that was --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, listen to me. Listen to what I'm asking you. The word "Kuber," does it denote a mountain?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that that mountain stretches from the Vitez municipality into the Busovaca municipality?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to your free assessment, how long or wide is that mountain?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Several kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your testimony, when you say that you went to Kuber, do you mean that you went to one particular spot which is located on Mount Kuber?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Unless I'm mistaken, you described this place as Gola Kosa?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, a little above Gola Kosa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, please look at the map on your right-hand side and indicate where Gola Kosa is or where your position was exactly.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: This is Gola Kosa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were a little above it, is that right, a little higher up?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, quite a bit higher up. Perhaps a kilometre or more higher up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So underneath the "K" for Kuber, the "K" for Mount Kuber?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And looking at it from the south-east, that is right on the map, the mountain stretches towards Busovaca; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you were telling us about your shift at Kuber, Mr. Santic, this relates to that location where you actually were?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you do not know who was, say, four kilometres away from you on that same mountain?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or two kilometres away from you?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or who was on Mount Kuber in the Busovaca municipality?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No, I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were further asked about an incident which occurred, and I think that there was a slight misunderstanding over that. You told us that on the 13th you arrived and took up your position at Kuber; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that one or two days later, that you heard shooting from the direction of Bilivode?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was before the 16th, was it not?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, before the 16th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that, later on, you heard that during this shooting one person was killed and two people were wounded?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, I heard that someone was wounded and that one man was wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that was before the 16th?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, before the 16th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: An incident was brought up that took place at the end of 1992 on which occasion a young Muslim was killed?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that word of this incident which took place at the -- on the main road below the village of Ahmici at the Catholic cemetery, was that it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true that it wasn't an incident between you villagers but an incident, as you said, the army that passed by there?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the army came from which was moving along that road?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Well, it came from Busovaca, from up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, and the Trial Chamber has already heard testimony about this, that on the occasion a member of the HVO was killed?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: On that occasion?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know about that or not?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But at any rate, it wasn't an incident which was linked to the neighbouring villages and the neighbouring villagers.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt. Nearly all the questions are of a leading and tendentious nature, and it really isn't very helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I shall abide by that criticism and try to put my questions in a different way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked, Mr. Santic, about some individuals which the military police brought to your defence lines for the purpose of trench-digging. I asked you and you told me that they were brought and taken away by the military police, but the military police was not present while they were doing the actual digging; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, those people were under guard on their journey out and their journey back. But what about their situation when they were up at the front line?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: They could move about quite normally and work quite normally. They had breakfast and lunch with us, had the same food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your father was among them, was he not?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Santic, you were shown a document, which was in fact an order by Colonel Blaskic, which describes the positions to be taken up by the Vitez Brigade. For reference purposes, this was document Z699. I should like to draw your attention, first of all, to the title of the document. It was sent, among others, to the 4th Battalion of the military police, the 4th Military Police Battalion. On the position you were located at, did you ever see a member of the military police as a defence of that position?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No. They would just come with the people coming up in the work platoons, and then they would go back and come back to fetch them in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But not in any fighting capacity, combat capacity.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Another question in that regard. Point 1 speaks of the formation of a defence line in the area of Kuber with the forces of the Vitez Brigade starting out from - please take a look at the map on your right-hand side - the village of Vidovici. Point to the village of Vidovici for us, please.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Then feature 514.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And feature 646, I don't know if you can see it. But you can see the village of Jelinak. Point the village of Jelinak out to us.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: This is Loncari, and Jelinak is a little further above.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There we have it.

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: And above Jelinak we have Obla Glava.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Santic, that these places, Obla Glava and Jelinak, are in the Busovaca municipality?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that you were at the Gola Kosa position. Is it obvious, then, Mr. Santic, to whom this order refers? Was it to your group of seven persons, or did it refer to somebody else?

utterances.speaker: VLADO SANTIC
utterances.text: Probably to somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I think I have exhausted all my questions. Thank you for your answers, Mr. Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Santic, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it. You are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, we've put off dealing with the documents. It might be convenient to deal with them now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Unless Judge Robinson is going to be back this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He will be.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It will be more convenient between the second and third witness. I don't think that the second witness is going to take very long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If it's a matter which we should all hear, of course we'll do it this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think it would probably be preferable for Judge Robinson to hear it directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you will permit me while we are waiting for the witness. We will use four documents with that witness, describing the events she will be talking about. Probably it would be better if I give it to the registrar; we may spare a minute or two for distribution. Then I will just identify the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you would like to take a seat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Examined by Mr. Kovacic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mrs. Grabovac. Thank you for responding to our invitation to come here. For the record, would you please state your name and surname clearly, your date and place of birth.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: My name is Ljubica Grabovac. I am from Vitez. I was born on the 16th of March, 1955, in the village of Cukle, Travnik municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Grabovac, are you married, and do you have any children?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I am married, and I have two children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By nationality you are a?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: By nationality I'm a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of which faith?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: The Orthodox faith.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you currently working?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: At the moment I'm on the waiting list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you're a housewife at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you hope to find a job soon, once again?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I hope so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mrs. Grabovac, with respect to your particulars, you are obviously not what you in Vitez call a true person of Vitez; is that true?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you come to take up residence in Vitez, and why?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I began living in Vitez from April 1989, when I married.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that Kruscica is the largest place in the Vitez municipality after the town of Vitez itself?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to the national composition, what kind of place is Kruscica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Kruscica is a multiethnic village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which ethnicity is most prevalent in Kruscica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: The Muslims are the majority population, followed by the Croats, the Serbs, and there are some Romanies or Gypsies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we can see that the population was truly a mixed one.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When we speak about Kruscica, you locals, when you use that name, is it true that you include under the notion of Kruscica the whole of Kruscica? So if we look at the road going up towards the hill, which is the main part of Kruscica, you actually mean the surrounding areas, Sofa and Toljusici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To inform the Trial Chamber, because there were several questions about this, the area referred to as Rijeka is the borderline area bordering on Kruscica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since 1989 to the present day, what have you learned about -- where does Rijeka end and Kruscica begin? Is that a clearly defined boundary?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: As far as I know, it's not clearly defined, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when somebody says, "from the upper part of Rijeka," that could also mean from Kruscica; is that true?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or when they say, "from the lower part of Kruscica," that could actually mean Rijeka, couldn't it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as the distribution of the ethnic groups are concerned, are you able to tell us where they were in Kruscica, how they were distributed?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: In the upper part of Kruscica, there were mostly Muslims living there, and a smaller number of Croats. In lower Kruscica, there were Croats, Serbs, Romanies, and a smaller portion of Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The two villages of Bobasi and Fatina Vodica, are they considered to be parts of Kruscica as well?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that these hamlets, as you look from Kruscica towards town, that they are on the left flank of Kruscica? Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Looking towards town on the left-hand side. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't think that you established it, but I take it from the evidence that the lady lived in Kruscica. Perhaps you better get that straight.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm just coming to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Grabovac, now that we have described the area to all intents and purposes and the places that exist there, could you describe to us actually where you lived?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I lived at Kruscica number 3, that's my address, which is at the crossroads between the upper part and lower part of Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your house at that time, according to the administrative division, was undoubtedly in Kruscica because that's your address. But as you say, this is somewhere in the middle of the zone that is referred to as upper and lower Kruscica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I going too fast? That term upper and lower Kruscica, they are not official administrative names, are they?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They are terms used by the local inhabitants when describing this position?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, in order to determine the locality in greater detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And so that we do not have to come back to this, could you specify the location of Toljusici as against your house, your then house?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: On a hill above as you go from the town to the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us roughly how far is your house from the first house in the part to which the people refer as Toljusici, roughly?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Ten minutes on foot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct, Mrs. Grabovac, that on the 16th of April, 1993, to your knowledge, an open conflict broke out in the area in which you lived?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did the open conflict between the BH army and the HVO in the area in which you lived begin?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I wouldn't really know the exact answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But which day do you perceive as the beginning of the war in the area in which you lived?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: When the armed fighting broke out between Croats and Muslims, and one -- when one could not leave the town any longer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the date?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But would it be April 1993?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, that is taken as the official date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it jog your memory if I told you that it was the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Well, thereabouts, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And on that day when the conflict began, even if you cannot remember the date, what was the first thing that you heard that day? How did you learn that a conflict had begun?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I heard gunfire early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you establish, could you define the direction from which it came?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: To me, it sounded like coming from all directions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any gunfire in the immediate vicinity of your house?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, did you know what was going on from those first sounds that you heard?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the days that followed, did you hear about what Croats from the upper part of Kruscica had done when the conflict began?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they stay in Kruscica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All the Croats stayed in Kruscica, did they?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No. Excuse me, could you repeat what part of Kruscica do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The upper part of Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No, they had been expelled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about it or did you have an opportunity to talk about this with the group of HVO soldiers who were up there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you know when was that exactly?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I cannot really pinpoint the time but it was towards the end of spring or perhaps in the early days of summer 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in relation to the date of the beginning of the conflict, could you say, perhaps, if it was 5 days, 10 days, 15, 20 days, after a couple of days, or perhaps longer?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No, I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Not far from your house, there was a large garage which was -- which belonged to one Vinko Miskovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that garage, was it used as something that had been designated as a shelter before in case of an attack or something?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the time when the conflict began, did anyone come to the garage and put you there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No, it was people who had fled Kruscica, the upper part of Kruscica went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I was thinking about showing the witness a map but when I tried, witness really doesn't have orientation on the map so I'm skipping that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And how many, approximately how many people found themselves in that garage?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: About 50.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those were men, women, children or what?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Children, women and elderly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any able-bodied men?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We already talked about various localities. Could you tell us from what parts of Kruscica did those people -- had those people fled?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: From the upper part of Kruscica, Bobasi and Toljusici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Grabovac, could you tell us, when did the first UNHCR humanitarian convoy come, using the road through Kruscica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: It was some seven years ago. I cannot really give you the date. All I can say is that it was late May or early June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we shall agree late spring, early summer?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those convoys then continued coming regularly; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the frequency; once a week, once in two weeks, or how?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Well, as a rule, once a week, sometimes even more often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And the convoys were escorted?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did that, who escorted those convoys?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: UNPROFOR APCs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those were those painted white, were they?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they had conspicuous emblems of the United Nations, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there were soldiers under arms in them?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the APCs also have their own weapons, don't they?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the reaction of the population around there, and especially the refugees, to the arrival of those convoys?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: The reaction was not hostile. All we wanted was them to talk to us and give us some of the relief which we needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those men indignant that they were not getting any relief themselves?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: You mean refugees? Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And apart from refugees, you, the residents of that part of Kruscica, were you also indignant about it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know what was the destination of that humanitarian relief, who was it intended for?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, we did know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: It was the Muslim part of the population in Gornja Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps in a few words you could describe the reaction of the people. What did they do and how did they behave with regard to those convoys?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: When we could hear the sound of the UN APCs approaching followed by trucks with humanitarian aid, then a refugee or one of us, I mean the local population, we would inform others, and we would come out into the street to block the passage of those convoys so as to make them give us part of that humanitarian aid because those refugees were hungry, they were poorly clothed, and they needed to be fed. We, ourselves, did not have enough food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in those early days, did anyone extend any aid to those refugees?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No, only the locals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we could say neighbours?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, some neighbours, friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But was food in plentiful supply at that time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Generally, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned when you tried to describe the mood. How much was an egg at the time, if you had to buy it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: An egg was five marks, five German marks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One egg you mean?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: One egg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from the UNPROFOR escort, or rather from the leaders of those convoys, did you ask them to give some of the food to you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the reaction?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: They talked with us, but they could not give us anything. They could not promise us anything so that we were not given anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to you who came out to meet those convoys, did anyone outside the circle of people that you mentioned from the municipal authority or the military HVO component, did any one of them give you any instructions as to how to treat those convoys?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No. Nobody ever gave us any instructions. We all did it on our own spontaneously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the convoys continued to arrive?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you try to intercept every convoy?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: We did not succeed in that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it true that you did manage to stop some of them and some you didn't?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: And some we didn't because there were several routes into upper Kruscica, and I was only on that one access road, the main one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on that road, did it ever happen when, after a lot of talking, persuasion and so on and so forth, did you let convoys through or did they have to go back?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: In the beginning they had to go back, but later on we would let them through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in those negotiations, were those negotiations ever joined or participated by somebody who represented the municipality?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember who that was?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Mr. Pero Skopljak would come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what would he try to achieve?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: He tried to calm us and to talk us out of stopping those humanitarian convoys for Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you, perhaps, remember what kind of argument did he use in order to talk you out of doing that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: At that time, the International Community or whoever it was, the UNHCR or UNPROFOR put pressure on the civilian authorities that they should then put their pressure on us to let this humanitarian aid through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you heed to that Pero Skopljak's plea?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Because we needed humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that there were also some other routes leading into Kruscica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from your knowledge, how many options were there for the trucks to get into Kruscica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I know four roads leading into Kruscica. There are two roads through Kruscica, it is where I was, then via Rijeka, through Vranjska, and Mount Kruscica towards Novi Travnik. That is part of Novi Travnik controlled by the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first two routes that you mentioned, they are practically parallel. They go from the main road southward, that is, Kruscica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And both those roads are flanked by houses, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the third route, which is slightly roundabout via Rijeka, via Vranjska to Kruscica, is it also flanked by houses on both its sides?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But there are also parts which are not inhabited?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, there is mountain, forest where there are no people living.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And UNPROFOR APCs did usually use such paths?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I wouldn't really know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown this first document of the 26th of May, 1993 signed by Mr. Ivan Santic. [In English] I believe, Your Honour, I should give the explanation. As you can see, the original of the letter is not a typed document. It is written by hand by Mr. Santic, Ivan, at least as it says in the signature. And the first one on English, it is originally translated document at that time since it was sent to UNPROFOR in English. It is not our translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Grabovac, I showed you this letter yesterday or the day before yesterday when we talked. Does it reflect those interventions of the municipality, Mr. Skopljak?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In those critical days, did you hear the municipality tried to do something both with UNPROFOR and you to pacify you and, on the other hand, to prevail upon UNPROFOR to do something? Did you know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Only when we had a meeting with Pero Skopljak, yes. He said pressure was brought on him so pressure will be brought on us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Will the witness be shown the next document or, sorry, we need a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is D106/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the next document of the 22nd of June, signed by a group of women, it says in brackets, "(Women from the Hamlet of Toljusici)." It's a little bit different but we can go on this one. Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document D107/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Grabovac, will you please read it, and I have only one question to ask you about it. Would you conclude from its contents that it also refers to the events that you described to us?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It mentions the shelling from Kruscica, and according to the symmetry of this letter, it came in the wake of the humanitarian relief delivered in Kruscica. Could you tell us something about that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Well, that was another thing which really irked us. Apart from not getting us humanitarian aid, which we needed, every time the convoy would go back, that is, UNPROFOR and the UNHCR, every time they left, we would be shelled and other heavy artillery weapons would be turned on us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the rumours that spread among people regarding those shells? What link was established between those convoys and the shelling?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Well, we suspected that UNPROFOR representatives were delivering weapons to that part of Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know for certain that this was true?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No, not for certain. But we had reason to suspect that because they never gave us unarmed women an opportunity to see what was being transported in those trucks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that when you stopped the convoys, at least in some situations, you asked to be shown that it was food that was being transported?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was always refused?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, it was always refused.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When there was shelling, were any civilians killed or wounded?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: One was wounded and one was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did this influence the tension among the local people and the indignation they felt?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Well, it did affect the feelings of indignation. But the prevailing feeling was that we mothers had to look after the safety of our children, and that is why we would take them to safe places and we would often let those convoys pass through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the end, did you give up, and when was that? When did you give up trying to stop those convoys?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Well, when we saw that there was nothing we could achieve, that no help was brought to any of us by any of those trucks in spite of their promises, and our safety was threatened, that was when we gave up stopping those convoys. I think it was sometime in the middle of August 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's clear up one other point. You said that you were present at a meeting when Mr. Pero Skopljak was there. Do you remember that there were other meetings with the civilian authorities from Vitez, or any other authorities, in which some people participated and others did not? Were you present at any other meeting?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear of other meetings?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us now go back to this document. [In English] It is dated the 2nd of June. But in the header there's the title "Women of Toljusici Hamlet."

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document D108/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Grabovac, would you please take a look at this document, see what it contains. Look at the signatures, the time. Mrs. Grabovac, let me ask you first of all, is your signature among these eight signatures here?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know any of the names signed here?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that these are women who participated like you in these activities?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: If you had been given this document to sign at the time it was written, would you have signed it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you accept the claims made in this letter?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the sake of illustration, where was your husband at that time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: At work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your husband ever at the front line, defending the village?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We may need some of these details later. You said that you can recognise some of these names. Can you tell us which names you recognise? What persons --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Do we need all this detail, I wonder?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to contribute to the authenticity of the document. Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: At the moment, the authenticity has not been challenged. So why don't you allow that to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, okay. [Interpretation] We need not go into this any further. [In English] Can we have a number for the document?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I gave the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Oh, you did. I'm sorry. I would kindly ask that the last document be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Grabovac, we will show you another document. Would you please look at it in Croatian, and would you look at the title and items 1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document D108/2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I thought the last one was 108.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I'm sorry. D109/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that I'm due to make a short explanation. As you can see, we did not translate the other items after 3, so from 3 to 6, only the first two, because they are entirely irrelevant for that document. And we got the document only three days before, so we were simply not able to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Grabovac, you have seen the first two items. Do you agree that these items refer to the events you have spoken about?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you tell us, if you remember, on those occasions when you stopped the convoys, did the civilian police ever arrive and try to remove you from the road?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, they did come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your reaction to this?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Well, we tried to convince them too that we were right to be doing this, and everything ended in talks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you believe that the conclusion under number 2 was initiated by the letter from the women of Toljusici, asking for ammunition for their husbands who were defending the village?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear anything about the situation having improved in the defence of the village after these letters?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No, I never heard anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Mrs. Grabovac, did it ever happen that the HVO army intervened in your relations with the convoy?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: The HVO army never intervened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally know Mario Cerkez at that time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No, not personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where his family lived?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I know now. I'm not sure I knew it then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was it? Can you tell us in relation to the place where the convoys were stopped?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: You mean where they lived?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: It was some five or six houses further on from the spot where the convoys were stopped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see or hear the wife or mother of the accused Cerkez participating in the stopping of convoys?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I never heard of it. And we resented it a little.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that Mario Cerkez at that time was the commander of the Vitez Brigade, or had you heard about it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Well, I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So why did you resent this?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: For the simple reason that the refugees and we, the local population, were exposing our children and ourselves to danger, but certain people did not come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the end, madam, just one more question. Do you remember in any of these encounters with the convoys and the escorts of the convoys, did you talk to a tall, good-looking gentleman in a white uniform with the insignia of an Observer of the European Community, who introduced himself as Henk Morsink? Does that mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence of Mr. Kordic has no questions for this witness. Thank you. Cross-examined by Mr. Scott:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Grabovac, just a few questions for you. In your statement that was provided to us by counsel, I just wanted to confirm, you went into some detail in describing the ethnic makeup of Kruscica and the surrounding, if you will, hamlets or connected villages. And I just wanted to confirm with you in paragraph 2.1 you said that you made the point of saying that before the conflict started in April of 1993, that these various ethnic groups, this community, lived together in peace; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, concerning your statements about the letter that -- one of the last letters that counsel showed you about the supply of ammunition, an order that was felt to be necessary to return fire, that was the document, for the record, D108/2. I take it from that, would you confirm the accuracy of that letter, Mrs. Grabovac, that you had, in fact, some information, you had some knowledge of such military matters in the area as the supply or availability of ammunition and heavy weapons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I only had information I heard from others, from what people said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But in response to counsel's questions about, again, D108/2 which you indicated you were in agreement with and then, in fact, had you been given the opportunity, you would have signed the letter, the first paragraph makes reference to the need for ammunition and makes the statement having in mind, for instance, heavy arms. If it would help for you to have the document in front of you, I would certainly ask the usher to put it in front of you. My question to you, Mrs. Grabovac, again is: Does that not indicate information or knowledge by yourself and these eight women who signed, apparently who signed this document, of such matters? The need for an adequate quantity of ammunition and weapons, having in mind heavy weapons, in order to return fire? Yes, no?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Please, could you repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, I don't know that we're going to get very much further.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. I assume, Your Honour, that from the document itself the point is made and I'll move on. Before turning to the blockade and I can tell the Court, Mr. President, that my questions will be very short just by a matter of minutes, few minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we turn to the question of the blockade and the convoys, specifically, you mentioned this concern or suspicion that UNPROFOR or international vehicles were carrying or transporting ammunition to the, if you will, Muslim enclave, in Kruscica. Now, ma'am, did you ever see any actual evidence of that or was that just speculation?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I never personally saw any evidence because they never allowed us to look into the trucks transporting humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you know, ma'am, that, in fact, that was the policy of these international organisations such as UNPROFOR and UNHCR that they did not allow, as a matter of policy, their vehicles to be inspected? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: We didn't want to inspect UNPROFOR vehicles, but only the trucks carrying humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But to close on that, Mrs. Grabovac, you did not, in fact, ever see any ammunition being transported; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Grabovac, let me suggest to you, or in the terminology in the Court, let me put it to you, please, and I mean that in a polite way, if I can say that, that allowing for some moments when there might have been some spontaneity of action, wasn't it truth, ma'am, that the blockade of movement to blockade and stop the convoys was part of a premeditated and deliberate HVO policy; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: It is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I take it you're saying it's not correct based on these particular actions around Kruscica, but my question for the moment is broader, if you know. Did you know - at this time, I will not go into the evidence that the Court may recall, but there was various -- there was, in fact, an HVO policy or it was that the stopping of convoys, the stopping of humanitarian aid were used as a tool or device of HVO policy; were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of the fact, ma'am, that specifically in connection with the times that counsel has asked you about and these areas, that orders had been given, including by Colonel Blaskic himself, that all access into these villages, including Kruscica, be stopped and prevented. Were you aware of such orders?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm going to move through this very quickly but only to assist, Your Honour, I'm going to ask the usher put in front of the witness Z683.1, only as one example. Perhaps for ease of reference, it might be on the ELMO, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can have the B/C/S version as I see you do in front of you, ma'am. I'm directing your attention - for purposes of recall, Your Honour, the Court will recall this is an exhibit that's already been admitted where specifically an order to Mr. Cerkez, do you see that, ma'am, in the upper right part of the document on the first page it says to the commander, in your language it says to the commander of the HVO Brigade Vitez, Mr. M. Cerkez and Special Purpose Unit Tvrtko. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see in paragraph two that Mr. Cerkez -- these forces including those commanded by Mr. Cerkez were assigned to occupy the defence region, blockade villages, and prevent all entrances to and exits from the villages. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I apologise but could you tell me the paragraph again?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly. It's paragraph number two. Just the first sentence. Wasn't Mr. Cerkez, who you testified a moment ago about, that you were aware to be the commander of the Vitez Brigade at that time, wasn't Mr. Cerkez, in fact, ordered to stop all entrance to and exit from these villages, including in Kruscica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I can't tell you anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to disagree or -- just I'm one question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let counsel finish the question before any objection is raised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Simply the final question on the document is: Do you have any reason to think that that was not the case? Did you see actions taking place or anything in your experience, which you've talked about in some detail, and having a knowledge of a number of items, anything that would conflict that this was, in fact, Colonel Blaskic's orders to Mr. Cerkez? Are you aware of any information that would contradict that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: That is a military order. I was an ordinary housewife at the time and I still am, and I really can't tell you anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Did you see the HVO on the 16th of April blockading the village?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Did you see them doing anything on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That being the first day of the conflict, what did you see of it? You said you heard gunfire from all around. What did you actually see?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: When the fog lifted at about 10.00 or 11.00, you know that Vitez is a foggy town, I was able to see, from the direction of Ahmici, smoke, and that was all I saw that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You didn't see any fighting in Kruscica itself?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, just on this I'm not going to take the witness through it, but just on this question, the orders on this subject of blockade, I just simply refer the record also to Z2612.10 concerning various Blaskic orders on the 17th of April. If I could ask the witness -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: May I intervene at this point of time? I don't think that the witness, particularly after what the witness said, that she did not see earlier any military command is asked about military commands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What counsel is entitled to do is to put a document to a witness and say, "Read this. You were there on the 16th of April. Did you see anything consistent with the document?" It's not asking for a comment on the document. It's asking for some facts which arise from the document, and counsel is entitled to ask such a question. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Would I then just insist that the document when introduced and not accompanied by comment of the counsel is commented correctly. Because in this document which was shown to the witness, there was nothing about blocking the convoys UNHCR or similar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, no, Mr. Kovacic. What counsel put, and put quite fairly, and if he hadn't been fair I would have stopped him, was that there was an order to blockade the villages. Now, what he then asked was: "Did you see anything about a blockade in Kruscica?" It wasn't an unfair question. If it had been so, I would have stopped him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Moving on, if the witness could just be shown only momentarily Exhibit Z894.1. That's the only document out of the ones of the several, of only four that I've even mentioned, I've already mentioned two of the four that is a new exhibit, Your Honour. The others have all been admitted before. While that's being distributed, Your Honour, I will say for the benefit of counsel, given the last objection, that the exercise here will be exactly the same. I will not be asking for the witness to state any opinion about the content of this document but, based on certain facts in the document, ask about her knowledge of events. If the English could be put on the ELMO, please, and the -- perhaps we can read it to her if there isn't. I will read it out loud and perhaps translation can help us for the witness. For Court and counsel, I'm referring to the top of the second page. For the record, there is a milinfosum dated the 8th of May, 1993. I'm referring now to the first paragraph on the second page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Grabovac, if you could please listen for the interpretation and then I'll ask you a couple of questions about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mrs. Grabovac, so you can follow, what is being put is a document which was prepared by UNPROFOR. It's an internal document. You won't be asked to comment on it because you've never seen it, never heard of it. What you will be asked about is the facts. So if you listen now, you'll hear what the soldiers reported.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "In the afternoon, a similar meeting was held for the Vitez area with Mario Cerkez and representatives from both the Kruscica and Preocica Battalions of 325 BiH Brigade in attendance. This meeting was extremely heated and turned upon the issues of prisoners, ethnic cleansing, and the restriction of freedom of movement occasioned by sniping attacks. Both sides implicitly acknowledged that their soldiers had conducted ethnic cleansing. They reluctantly agreed to attempt to effect a cease-fire from..." Now, have you been able to hear that in translation, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on your involvement in this area during the spring and summer of 1993, my statement to you or my question to you is this: Do you agree with the assessment that during this time period about this location that both the Muslim side, if you will, and the HVO side were engaged in and had engaged in ethnic cleansing?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I can't tell you anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, one more question before moving on similar to the question about the prior document. Were you aware, and can you tell this Court of any information or knowledge you might have which would contradict this assessment apparently concerning a meeting involving Mr. Cerkez in which, apparently, at least as reported, both sides acknowledged that their soldiers had conducted ethnic cleansing? Did you see anything happening in the area where you lived in Kruscica during the spring and summer of 1993 that would contradict or be contrary to this assessment?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I can't tell you anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Counsel asked you about an ECMM monitor by the name of Morsink. Did you have any knowledge that in a meeting with Mr. -- between Mr. Morsink and Mr. Cerkez on the 18th of April, 1993, that Mr. Cerkez threatened to destroy Muslim houses in the area --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't think the witness can deal with that. She has no knowledge of Mr. Morsink at all and wouldn't have any knowledge of such a meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following counsel's earlier question, ma'am, if I can just clarify, you have no knowledge of Mr. Morsink or ECMM's involvement in the Kruscica area; is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, on the 17th of April - I'm pointing out facts, but it's only facts that I'll ask you about - there was evidence, I'll just remind the Court, from Mr. Morsink that he attempted to enter Kruscica on the 17th of April and it was blocked by soldiers and mines. Now, were you aware of that, Ms. Grabovac, that on the 17th of April, the entrance into Kruscica was blocked by HVO soldiers and mines, as opposed to civilian women and children?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I take it, Ms. Grabovac, you're not suggesting that the women and children placed mines on the road, are you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Could you repeat that question, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you've indicated that there were these blockades by women and children civilians of convoys, and I've indicated to you, and the Court will recall the evidence itself, that on the 17th of April, it's been reported that the road into Kruscica was blocked by soldiers and mines. My question to you, ma'am, is: You're not suggesting, are you, that the women and children put mines on the road? Are you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I don't know anything about those mines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Grabovac, isn't it true that, generally speaking, these so-called blockades by civilians were, at least on most occasions, closely orchestrated and supported by the HVO forces; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: The blockades that I took part in were not orchestrated by anyone. It was a spontaneous blockade by women and children who were hungry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me indicate another incident to you, and to remind the Court. On the 17th of May, a month later, a British officer named Major Bower again was attempting to enter through the blockade of Kruscica, attempted to walk through the crowd in front of his vehicle, and HVO soldiers on both sides of the road opened fire, shooting over his head. Now, were you present on that occasion, or did you hear about it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: None of the women and children that you were associated with at the time, for instance, again these eight women who signed this other document, none of them reported to you about such an incident; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My final couple of questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the following day, on the 18th of May, Major Bower attempted to enter Kruscica again, and on that day reported that the road into Kruscica was blocked by mines. Now, were you aware of that, Ms. Grabovac?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My final question is: Again, I take it you're not suggesting that the civilians put mines on the road, are you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I don't know whether there were any mines at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If there were mines on the road, if Major Bower's report is accurate, do you have any information or knowledge that it was the women and children who put the mines on the road?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No, I have no information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Re-examined by Mr. Kovacic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Grabovac, I'd like to clarify some points, if I may. Is it correct that, as a rule, every time the UNHCR vehicles brought aid to Kruscica and when they went back, that there would be shelling in your part of the village soon afterwards?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told us that you cannot claim that UNPROFOR was, in fact, taking weapons to Kruscica. But did you believe that it was just by chance that once the UNHCR was returning you were shelled?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No, that was not by accident, by chance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You were shown the first document by the Prosecution, the order by Blaskic to Cerkez, Z683.1, I believe. Did you notice the date on that document, what the period was?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Well, even if I saw the date, I don't remember it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, Mrs. Grabovac, whether in all your life, up until the present day, you ever saw or held a military order in your hands.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, please, since the beginning of the conflict, up until the Washington Agreements, did you ever see in the part of the village that you reside in, around your own house, whether there was any actual fighting, actual combat activity taking place?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question. Be clearer, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next to the house you live in, a few houses to your left and right, so around the area of your house, was there any direct military action, armies?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Well, only the shelling, and in January 1994 the attack from Kruscica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Repeated shelling.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, shelling, and an armed attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you said that that was when?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: In January 1994, as far as I remember, on the 8th or 9th of January, 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, then, that in the course of 1993, in the vicinity of your home, you never saw any soldiers, armed soldiers whatsoever engaging in combat action?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I did not see them in combat action, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. From the knowledge you gained or the information you had, can you tell us where the nearest places -- how far away from your own house was the demarcation line between the HVO and the other side?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: I learnt that only later on, after the war, that it was 150 metres, as the crow flies, from my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the war, could you ever approach those localities?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You were also asked several questions about ethnic cleansing. Do you know what the term "ethnic cleansing" in fact means? How would you define ethnic cleansing? Could you explain the term to us?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Well, my free assessment, that is, in my own view, that probably means expelling people of a certain nationality away from a certain region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. As a woman who lived in that area, were you ever able to conclude that anybody was expelling Serbs from the territory in a planned, organised manner?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever able to conclude that somebody was expelling the Muslims from the area in the same way?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. As we're discussing this point, and taking the example of religion as a characteristic, where was your nearest church, that is to say, the Orthodox church? You said that you yourself were an Orthodox. Where was your nearest church?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: In Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which means some 15 kilometres away from your house; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the nearest mosque for the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: There were several. The nearest one, I think, was in a place called Mahala, upper Vitez, two kilometres away from my own house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there a mosque in Gornja Kruscica as well?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it have a minaret?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the war, did you ever happen to see that mosque?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it still exists there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Can I correct myself on one point, please? After the war, I didn't see that mosque. But I can hear prayers going on every morning from the minaret.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: How does this arise from the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Ethnic cleansing, Your Honour. I think that having a minaret in the middle of the village is a kind of symbol.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you could bring the examination to an end. It's after the adjournment time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I have two or three short questions more. Nothing else, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were asked about mines on the road. Let's make one point clear. If you were to go from your house towards the main road, towards Vitez, were there any blockades in any way on that road?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or obstacles?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any obstacles in the form of mines?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No, there were no mine blockades.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able, madam, in the course of 1993, to start walking along the road uphill towards Gornja Kruscica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't able to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Because of the fighting and daily shelling that was going on from that part. It was dangerous; you couldn't just walk around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So higher up along the road from your house, you never took that road.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether there were any mines on the road, or blockades or obstacles of any kind?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever ask anybody whether there were any blockades on that part of the road?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: No, because I wasn't interested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know, Madam Grabovac, whether somewhere higher up from your house, moving towards upper Kruscica, on that road, whether there was a demarcation line between the two sides?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA GRABOVAC
utterances.text: Well, I learnt of that only later on.
